subject: Follow-up & next steps: token economics, host comparisons (Acme Retail)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-22T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up & next steps: token economics, host comparisons (Acme Retail)

Hi Liam — great to chat earlier today. Quick recap and the items we promised to follow up on from our discovery: 

Summary of what you shared
- Primary use case: in-product assistant for customer support and search enrichment. Expected steady-state: ~1.5B tokens/month, with occasional peaks up to ~40M tokens/day during campaigns.
- Latency SLO: 300–400ms p95 for short-turn queries.
- Data residency: US; no PII in prompts stored beyond 30 days.

What you asked for
- Ballpark unit economics: target $/1M tokens for hosted inference vs reserved/dedicated and self-hosted options.
- Direct comparison vs OpenAI/Anthropic and typical open-host providers.
- Example SOW and a pilot plan to validate costs/perf.

Attached I dropped a short spreadsheet (redwood-token-comparison-1m.xlsx) with three scenarios: Hosted (pay-as-you-go), Dedicated (committed capacity), and Private (self-host + partner-host). I also attached a one-page SOW draft to kick off procurement if you want to move quickly.

Assumptions used in the spreadsheet (high-level)
- Tokenization rate: 1.25 tokens/word average; avg call = 1.2K tokens (prompt + response) for the assistant flows you described.
- KV cache & prefix caching applied for repeated context; expected token efficiency improvement ~15% on response tokens.
- Dedicated pricing assumes a 12-month commit with standard burst allowance.

High-level guidance (ballpark numbers; exact quote will depend on model & sequence length distribution)
- Redwood hosted (baseline): $85–95 per 1M tokens; with a 12-month committed tier we can get to ~$60/1M with the volumes you mentioned.
- OpenAI: public list tends to be higher for larger models (rough ballpark for comparable capabilities: $150–220/1M depending on model and compute backend).
- Anthropic: in the same ballpark as OpenAI for higher-capability models (~$120–200/1M).
- Self-host / other open-model hosts: nominal infra-only unit costs can be $30–80/1M depending on quantization, instance utilization, and specialist runtime work — but operational overhead and engineering time should be included.

Next steps I propose
1) Confirm monthly avg vs peak for the next 6 months (so we can prepare a Dedicated capacity plan).
2) If procurement is ready, I can share a draft SOW and a 2-week pilot plan (100M tokens) to validate performance and actual unit cost.
3) Karthik (copied) will prepare a committed-tier pricing worksheet based on your final traffic profile.

If that looks right, can you confirm: 1) the 1.5B/month estimate (or correct number), 2) who should receive the formal SOW (procurement@acmeretail.com?), and 3) preferred timing for a pilot (next two weeks vs April)?

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up & next steps: token economics, host comparisons (Acme Retail)

Thanks, Liam — great context and thank you for the budget band. Short answers and a little more color on assumptions so procurement/legal have what they need for review.

Redwood baseline explanation (assumptions behind $85–95/1M)
- Model class: our baseline uses a mid-to-high capability open model we host (comparable to a 30B-ish parameter family with latency optimizations). If you pick a higher-capability proprietary model, list prices trend up.
- Effective token length: pricing assumes average call ~1.2K tokens (input + output). If your average is significantly lower, unit $/1M improves.
- Observability & tracing: standard console & 30-day traces included in Hosted pricing. Extended retention and premium audit logs are add-ons (we call that Redwood Observe+).
- Network egress: outbound data transfer for typical API responses is included in the hosted line item for US regions; large file attachments or streaming video would be extra.
- Caching effects: we model ~15% reduction in token usage from prefix/KV caching for repeated context; if your usage has lower cache hit rates, expect higher realized token counts.

Direct comparisons (illustrative per 1M tokens) — ballpark numbers to help your finance model:
- Redwood (Hosted, PAYG): $85–95/1M
- Redwood (Dedicated, 12m commit): $55–65/1M (volume to reach this: ~1B+/mo)
- OpenAI (public higher-capability endpoints): $140–220/1M depending on model and negotiated enterprise discounts
- Anthropic (Claude-like comparable): $120–200/1M
- Typical cloud-hosted open-model stack (infra + ops): $30–80/1M (lower nominal cost but you should add ops engineering, reliability, SRE on-call cost, and ongoing upgrade work)

Why Redwood could be a more predictable choice
- We include serving runtime optimizations and model-specific kernel selection that improve tokens/sec and reduce total instance count required.
- Smart routing + KV caching reduces billable tokens in many assistant scenarios compared to raw API calls against a managed model.
- Dedicated commitments give you the lowest unit costs while keeping our operational SLAs.

Recommended next steps
- I will turn the spreadsheet into a short one-page appendix showing per-scenario assumptions for the SOW.
- Proposed pilot: April 6–20, 2026, 100M tokens (subset of traffic) — we run the pilot on Redwood Hosted and, if you prefer, we can spin a short-lived Dedicated pool to measure real committed performance.
- Karthik, could you assemble two committed-tier price points (12m, 24m) and an internal approval note for a potential $/1M floor at ~ $60 for 12m?

I'll update the attachments and include the explicit data retention language for procurement/legal. Anything else you need in the SOW besides residency and retention?

Best,
Vanessa
